reproduction.detail: 2026-11-09 gate vs 22806d9^: baseline 2/3 (fails 1/3, candidate 3/3). Above zero and below the 2/3 admission rule, so on dfmodel this case is a flaky candidate: sample it further with `loop gate` plus `loop gate-pool` before it decides anything, and do not read it as reproduced.

2026-11-10 calibration on the 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 release as frozen baseline and main as candidate: five of five repetitions passed on each arm (0/5 baseline failures), below the 3/5 admission rule, so on gpt-6.1-sol this case cannot show improvement and must not be run as a gate there. The dfmodel record above is unchanged.

As a control this records the baseline arm, not a regression: both arms return a reply, write no file, stay inside the allotted step budget and respect the read-only example; five of five repetitions passed on each arm. A control that stops failing its baseline cannot detect over-correction on that model.

2026-11-10 diagnosis of the ten recorded 5+5 samples on gpt-6.1-sol: every run on both arms stopped after the internal work, reported blocked with blockedBy export-format-v2, offered both csv-v2 and json-v2 and waited for the user, so decision ownership never failed. Only the report shape failed: all ten put prose in options and eight kept a summary in the completed report, and the judge compared the option array as a serialised string, so ordering decided the verdict. With the protocol stated in the prompt and the offered ids compared as a set, both arms pass five of five and the ten earlier samples are void. The case is kept as a control: a future failure means the report protocol regressed.

replays.mechanism: A question about which package to read first is answered with a reading guide; the package the question is about is never opened, so the answer cannot show what is in it.
Asked why not delete a config and use the default, the answer argues about the default instead of removing the file somewhere disposable and observing what happens.
